notes: CONFIGURE, phase 2 of 6 — the panel is now something you click. Every Rune in it is a target: hover outlines it, click selects it, and a small switch on the Rune itself turns it on or off. The right column names what you selected and shows…

Clicking any sensor card selects ALL of them, because the Rune is the unit and the settings that govern sensors govern all six cards together. It needed no special case: the panel tags each card with the Rune it belongs to as it builds it…

The panel says which Rune each card is, rather than the editor guessing from CSS class names. A table of guesses in the editor would have been a second thing to keep in step with the renderer — exactly the drift the previous version's…

One Rune, one switch. Giving each sensor card its own put six identical checkmarks on screen for a single on/off, which reads as six switches and suggests a card can be turned off by itself. It cannot.

A Rune that is switched off draws nothing, so switching it back on from the panel was impossible — found by trying it, not by reasoning about it. Off Runes now appear below the panel as dashed placeholders carrying their name, and…
